page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyperthreading enabled. The instance is configured with 360 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25%, indicating lower clock speeds or older architectural efficiency per thread. However, multi-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with both cached and uncached read-only operations, as well as large block write operations, ranking in the top 25%. Database operations and static web serving throughput perform at average levels, while Redis SET operations demonstrate strong throughput at 62.03 million operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, the n1-standard-96 offers a massive allocation of vCPUs and memory on a mature hardware platform. The primary tradeoff is the weak single-threaded performance and lack of modern instruction sets like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX, which limits its efficiency for modern AI text generation workloads. However, for highly parallelized legacy workloads that can leverage all 96 vCPUs and benefit from high memory bandwidth without requiring local NVMe storage, this instance provides a stable, high-capacity environment.

This instance is best suited for highly multi-threaded general-purpose workloads. Appropriate use cases include large-scale web serving, parallel software compilation, database operations, and high-throughput caching layers like Redis. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or real-time LLM text generation.
